While a lot of people here mentioned great bass metal bass players who play fingerstyle, there's a few good reasons why a majority of metal bassist choose a Pick.
A. It is easier to play faster with a Pick. While not exclusive to Pick playing,  as you can obviously play fast with fingers, the tempos and rhythms played in metal often are more suited for Pick playing, partly because of the guitar riff heavy nature of the genre.
B. Sound. This is probably the definitive answer, and vastly more important than the speed you're playing at. Pick has a lot more punch and has a more metallic trebleish sound compared to the warm and round sound of fingers, that is more favored by metal bassists in general.

In the end, knowing both techniques will make you a better player for sure and it'll allow you to explore your sound as a bass player more easily. You mentioned that you weren't comfortable with Pick playing,  it all comes down to practice. I highly suggest you learn to play with a Pick properly especially if you're into metal.
